div.head: ECf 11.1 B 2
div.ab: Suscepistis enim nuper miseratione diuina in regno Britannie legem et fidem Christi, habetis penes uos in regno utramque paginam, ex illis Dei gratia per consilium regni uestri sume legem, et per illam Dei patientia uestrum rege Britannie regnum!
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 636 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 11, 1, and numbers 11, 1 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 11, 1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
div.ab: For you have lately received, by divine compassion, in the kingdom of Britain the law and faith of Christ; you have with you in the kingdom both pages (the two Testaments); from them, by the grace of God, through the counsel of your kingdom take a law, and through it, by God's forbearance, rule your kingdom of Britain!
